# Heimdall documentation (full text)

> Every page of the Heimdall docs in one file, for language models and agents. Index: https://heimdall.fund/llms.txt. API spec: https://api.heimdall.fund/openapi.json.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs

---
description: >-
  Heimdall is the guardian layer for onchain agents on Robinhood Chain. Three
  products share one rule: nothing gets signed unchecked.
---

# Build with Heimdall

Heimdall runs on Robinhood Chain mainnet (chain ID 4663).

| Product | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [Shield](shield/transactions.md) | Simulate and judge any transaction before your agent signs it. |
| [Signature checks](shield/signatures.md) | Catch Permit and Permit2 drainers that never touch the chain. |
| [Vaults](products/vaults.md) | Run depositor money that can only trade with a Shield receipt. |
| [Signals](products/signals.md) | Buy or sell market signals per call, paid in USDG. |

## Quickstart: protect an agent in 2 minutes

**1. Install the SDK.**

```bash
npm install @heimdallfund/sdk viem
```

**2. Replace your agent's `sendTransaction` with `guardedSend`.** It asks Shield first and only sends on ALLOW.

```ts
import { HeimdallShield, guardedSend, HeimdallDenied } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

const shield = new HeimdallShield({ apiKey: process.env.HEIMDALL_API_KEY }); // key optional on the free plan

try {
  const { hash } = await guardedSend(wallet, { to, data, value }, {
    shield,
    policy: { strict: true, maxNativeOut: "50000000000000000" }, // 0.05 ETH per tx
  });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof HeimdallDenied) console.log(e.result.findings); // why it was blocked
}
```

**3. Check signatures too.** Before your agent signs a message (Permit, Permit2, marketplace order):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.heimdall.fund/v1/check-signature \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "signer": "0xYourAgent", "typedData": { "domain": {…}, "types": {…}, "primaryType": "Permit", "message": {…} } }'
```

{% hint style="info" %}
No SDK? Everything is plain HTTP. See [Transaction checks](shield/transactions.md) for the full request and response.
{% endhint %}

## How the pieces fit

1. An agent builds a transaction (a swap, an approval, a transfer).
2. **Shield** simulates it on the latest Robinhood Chain block and answers ALLOW, WARN or DENY with reasons and an EIP-712 receipt valid for 120 seconds.
3. A **vault** only executes a manager's trade when it carries a fresh ALLOW receipt, and checks trade size and loss with price feeds.
4. Agents buy their edge from **Signals**, paying per call with gasless vouchers.

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/limits

description: Shield is free to start. Keys lift the limits; $HEIM holders get more for free.

# API keys & limits

| Plan | Per minute | Per day |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free (no key) | 30 checks per IP | 1,000 checks per agent wallet |
| Free + $HEIM holder | 30 checks per IP | 5,000 checks per agent wallet |
| API key | 600 checks per key | No daily cap; metered at $0.001 per check |

The holder minimum is 100,000 $HEIM in the agent wallet, checked onchain. No staking or lock-up.

## Getting a key

Sign in with your wallet at [heimdall.fund/app/keys](https://heimdall.fund/app/keys), create a key and copy it: Heimdall stores only its hash. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer hd_live_…` or `x-api-key`. Revoke it any time on the same page.

## Response headers

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `x-ratelimit-limit` / `x-ratelimit-remaining` | Per-minute budget. |
| `x-heimdall-quota-remaining` | Free checks left today for this wallet. |
| `x-heimdall-holder` | `true` when the $HEIM holder quota applied. |
| `retry-after` | Seconds to wait after a 429. |

# Security

## Reviews

| Review | Scope | Found | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Review 1 | Vaults, Signals, factory, Shield guard | 1 critical, 2 high, 6 medium, 5 low, 6 info | All critical, high and medium fixed |
| Review 2 | Heimdall Pay, staking, fee splitter, stock price feed | 1 medium, 5 low, 7 info | Medium and lows fixed or accepted |
| Review 3 | All contracts: stateful invariant testing, ERC-4626 views, production build size | 2 low | Both fixed |
| Review 4 | Risk Oracle, Guard for Safe (Safe module), x402 facilitator, Agent Passport | 1 medium, 2 low | All fixed |
| Addendum | Auto-Invest | 2 low, 3 info | Lows fixed |

Every attack found is kept as a regression test. The contracts have 143 tests, including 15 fuzz properties and 14 stateful invariants (10,000 fuzz runs and 512 random sequences of 200 actions before each release), and Slither static analysis. An independent audit comes next; its full report will be published when it is done.

## Independent audit

The contracts go to an independent audit firm. The audit pack is ready in the repository (`contracts/audit/`): scope with file hashes, threat model, invariants, known issues and every internal review. The full report will be published, with every finding and how it was fixed.

## How to report

Email **security@heimdall.fund** with the steps or a proof of concept, ideally a test against a fork of Robinhood Chain. We reply within 48 hours.

Test on a local fork only and keep the issue private until it is fixed. If you follow these rules, we will not take legal action over your research.

# Transaction checks

Send the transaction your agent is about to sign. Shield runs it against the latest block with `eth_simulateV1` and tells you exactly what would happen.

## Request

```http
POST https://api.heimdall.fund/v1/check
Authorization: Bearer hd_live_…        (optional on the free plan)
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "chainId": 4663,
  "from": "0xAgentWallet",
  "to": "0xTargetContract",            // null to deploy a contract
  "data": "0x…",
  "value": "0",                         // wei, decimal or 0x-hex
  "policy": { … }                       // optional, see below
}
```

## Response

```json
{
  "checkId": "0x51705c…",
  "verdict": "DENY",
  "riskScore": 90,
  "summary": ["Calls approve(address,uint256) on USDG (0x5fc5…d168)", "Approves unlimited USDG → 0x3333…3333"],
  "findings": [{ "code": "UNLIMITED_APPROVAL_TO_EOA", "severity": "deny", "message": "…" }],
  "approvals": [ … ],
  "assetChanges": [{ "symbol": "USDG", "delta": "-100000000", "kind": "erc20", … }],
  "simulation": { "ok": true, "available": true, "gasUsed": "46213" },
  "receipt": { "signer": "0x…", "signature": "0x…", "expiresAt": 1795400000, "message": { … } }
}
```

`verdict` is `ALLOW`, `WARN` or `DENY`; `riskScore` runs 0–100. A WARN stays a WARN unless the policy sets `strict`; then every WARN becomes DENY. Vaults only accept receipts whose verdict is ALLOW.

## Policy

| Field | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `strict` | Every WARN becomes DENY. |
| `allowTargets` | If set, the target must be in this list. |
| `denyTargets` | Targets that are always denied. |
| `maxNativeOut` | Per-transaction cap for ETH leaving the wallet, in wei. |
| `maxTokenOut` | Per-transaction cap per token, raw units, keyed by token address. |
| `trustedSpenders` | Unlimited approvals to these spenders do not warn. |
| `denyUnlimitedApprovals` | Unlimited approvals are always denied. |
| `trustedRecipients` | Sending assets to these does not raise `ONE_WAY_OUTFLOW`. |
| `trustedDelegates` | EIP-7702 delegate contracts the agent may authorise beyond the wallet implementations Heimdall knows. |
| `allowContractDeploy` | Allow `to = null`. |

## Findings

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SIM_REVERTED` | deny | The transaction would revert; the reason is decoded. |
| `UNLIMITED_APPROVAL_TO_EOA` / `APPROVAL_TO_EOA` | deny / warn | Approval (ERC-20, Permit2, setApprovalForAll) to an address with no code. |
| `UNLIMITED_APPROVAL` | warn | Unlimited approval to an untrusted contract, also inside multicall and Universal Router batches. |
| `HONEYPOT` | deny | A token you receive cannot be transferred again, or cannot be sold back to the pool it came from. |
| `VANISHING_TOKEN` | deny / warn | A token arrives and is taken out of the wallet in the same transaction (denied when you paid for it). |
| `ALLOWANCE_BYPASS` | deny | A stranger, or the token's `owner()`, can `transferFrom` your wallet with no allowance: tokens can be clawed back. |
| `FAKE_TOKEN` | deny / warn | The symbol (deny) or name (warn) of a known token such as USDG, WETH or a stock token, at a different address. Look-alike letters and zero-width characters are folded first. |
| `HOOK_TAKES_DELTA` | warn | A Uniswap v4 pool on the route has a hook that can change swap amounts: a hidden fee of any size. |
| `HOOK_DYNAMIC_FEE` | warn | A Uniswap v4 pool whose hook sets the swap fee at swap time. |
| `HOOK_ON_SWAP` | info | A v4 hook runs on every swap and could refuse later trades. |
| `HOOK_NO_CODE` / `BLOCKLISTED_HOOK` | deny | The pool names a hook with no contract, or a known malicious one. |
| `LOOKALIKE_ADDRESS` | deny | A target, recipient or spender that shares 3+ first and last characters (8+ in total) with a known address, a trusted one in your policy, or one this wallet already used: address poisoning. |
| `TRANSFER_TAX` | info / warn / deny | A received token loses value on transfer (≥5% warns, ≥50% denies). |
| `NATIVE_LIMIT` / `TOKEN_LIMIT` | deny | Above a policy cap. |
| `DRAINS_BALANCE` | warn | Moves 90% or more of the wallet's balance of an asset. |
| `ONE_WAY_OUTFLOW` | warn | Assets leave to an untrusted address and nothing comes back. |
| `BLOCKLISTED_TARGET` / `SPENDER` / `RECIPIENT` / `TOKEN` | deny | A known drainer or exploit address is involved, or the token being bought is a known scam. |
| `ZERO_TARGET` | deny | Sending to the zero address. |
| `TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED` / `DENYLISTED_TARGET` | deny | Outside the policy's allow list, or on its deny list. |
| `EOA_WITH_DATA` | warn | Calldata sent to an address with no code. |
| `SIM_UNAVAILABLE` | warn | The simulator could not run; nothing is assumed safe. |
| `DELEGATED_EOA`, `KNOWN_CONTRACT`, `APPROVAL_REVOKE` | info | Context only. |

## Receipts

Each verdict is signed as EIP-712 with domain `{ name: "Heimdall Shield", version: "1", chainId }` and type:

```
Receipt(address agent, address target, bytes32 dataHash, uint256 value, uint8 verdict, uint64 expiresAt, bytes32 checkId)
```

`GET /v1/signer` returns the current signer address. Heimdall vaults accept a receipt once, only before it expires, and only for exactly the same call.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/signatures

---
description: >-
  POST /v1/check-signature: judge Permit, Permit2, Seaport and personal_sign
  requests before an agent signs them.
---

# Signature checks

Most drains today never start with a transaction: the victim signs a Permit or Permit2 message and the attacker submits it later. Check every signature request first.

## Request

```http
POST https://api.heimdall.fund/v1/check-signature

// EIP-712 (eth_signTypedData_v4) — pass the payload exactly as the app gave it
{ "chainId": 4663, "signer": "0xAgent", "typedData": { "domain": {…}, "types": {…}, "primaryType": "PermitSingle", "message": {…} } }

// personal_sign / eth_sign
{ "chainId": 4663, "signer": "0xAgent", "message": "0x…" }

// EIP-7702 authorization: the contract the wallet would delegate to
{ "chainId": 4663, "signer": "0xAgent", "authorization": { "chainId": 4663, "address": "0xDelegate", "nonce": 7 } }
```

## What is recognised

| Type | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| EIP-2612 Permit | Spender is a contract, amount, deadline, owner = signer. |
| DAI-style Permit | Spender and expiry (DAI permits are always unlimited). |
| Permit2 PermitSingle / PermitBatch | Every token, amount and expiration; spender. |
| Permit2 PermitTransferFrom (+ batch, witness) | Tokens, amounts, spender, deadline. |
| Seaport OrderComponents | Denies orders that give assets away for nothing; warns on any listing. |
| personal\_sign of a 32-byte hash | Denied: blind signing can authorise anything. |
| EIP-7702 authorization | Allowed only for known wallet implementations (MetaMask DeleGator, Simple7702Account, Uniswap Calibur, Coinbase EIP7702Proxy, Ambire) or ones in `trustedDelegates`. Denied for chain ID 0, another chain, an address with no code, a blocklisted contract or any unknown contract. The same rules apply to the `authorizationList` of a type 4 transaction sent to `/v1/check`. |
| Anything else | WARN: unrecognised typed data. |

## Findings

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PERMIT_TO_EOA` / `PERMIT_UNLIMITED_TO_EOA` | deny | A plain wallet could take your tokens. |
| `PERMIT_UNLIMITED` | warn (deny with policy) | Unlimited permit to an untrusted contract. |
| `PERMIT_LONG_EXPIRY` | warn | Valid for more than 30 days. |
| `WRONG_CHAIN` | deny | The signature is for another chain. |
| `ORDER_FOR_NOTHING` | deny | Marketplace order that pays you nothing. |
| `BLIND_HASH_SIGNATURE` | deny | Signing an opaque 32-byte hash. |
| `BLOCKLISTED_SPENDER` / `BLOCKLISTED_CONTRACT` | deny | Known malicious address. |
| `UNKNOWN_DELEGATE` | deny | EIP-7702: hands full control of the wallet to a contract Heimdall does not know. |
| `AUTH_ALL_CHAINS` | deny | EIP-7702 authorization with chain ID 0: valid on every chain. |
| `DELEGATE_NO_CODE` / `DELEGATE_IS_WALLET` / `BLOCKLISTED_DELEGATE` | deny | EIP-7702 delegate with no code yet, a delegated wallet, or a known malicious contract. |
| `KNOWN_DELEGATE` / `TRUSTED_DELEGATE` / `AUTH_REVOKE` | info | A known wallet implementation, one your policy trusts, or clearing the delegation. |

{% hint style="info" %}
The same policy fields as [transaction checks](transactions.md#policy) apply, for example `trustedSpenders` for your own router.
{% endhint %}

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/webhooks

---
description: Signed HTTPS events when Shield blocks one of your agents or a wallet you run gains a risky approval.
---

# Webhooks

Heimdall can POST to your server the moment Shield blocks one of your agents, or when a wallet you run picks up a risky approval. Every event is signed.

## Set up

1. Open [API keys & webhook](https://heimdall.fund/app/keys) and sign in with the wallet that owns your API keys.
2. Enter an HTTPS endpoint, pick the events, and list up to 20 wallets to watch (usually your agents' wallets).
3. Copy the signing secret (`whsec_…`). It is shown once; **New secret** replaces it.
4. Press **Send test event**. The last 20 deliveries are listed with their HTTP status.

## Events

| Type | When |
| --- | --- |
| `shield.deny` | A transaction or signature check made with one of your API keys returned DENY |
| `shield.warn` | The same, for WARN |
| `wallet.risky_approval` | A watched wallet gained a new Danger or Review approval (checked every 15 minutes) |
| `test` | Sent by the Send test event button |

## Payload

A JSON body with `id`, `type`, `createdAt` (UTC) and `data`. Headers: `heimdall-event`, `heimdall-delivery` and `heimdall-signature`.

```json
{
  "id": "evt_Qm3x…",
  "type": "shield.deny",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-23T14:02:11.402Z",
  "data": {
    "kind": "tx",
    "checkId": "0x9f…",
    "verdict": "DENY",
    "riskScore": 95,
    "findings": [{ "code": "BLOCKLISTED_TARGET", "severity": "deny", "message": "…" }],
    "chainId": 4663,
    "from": "0xYourAgent…",
    "to": "0xDrainer…",
    "apiKeyId": "a1b2c3d4e5f6"
  }
}
```

## Verify the signature

`heimdall-signature` is `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where the hex is HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` with your secret. Check it against the raw body before parsing, and reject events older than five minutes:

```typescript
import { parseWebhook } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

const event = await parseWebhook({ secret: process.env.HEIMDALL_WEBHOOK_SECRET!, body: rawBody, signature: req.headers.get("heimdall-signature") });
```

## Delivery rules

* Answer with any 2xx within 5 seconds. Redirects are not followed.
* Events are sent once and not retried; use `id` to drop duplicates.
* After 15 failed deliveries in a row the webhook is switched off. Saving it again switches it back on.
* Endpoints must be public HTTPS: localhost, private networks and credentials in the URL are refused.

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/wallet-check

---
description: See every live approval of a wallet, ranked by risk, and revoke the dangerous ones.
---

# Wallet Check

Wallet Check finds every live token approval of a Robinhood Chain wallet. It ranks each one by risk, shows how many dollars it exposes, and lets the owner revoke it. Checking is read-only and works for any address; only revoking sends a transaction.

## What it reads

* ERC-20 approvals (`approve`, `permit`)
* Permit2 allowances (expired ones are ignored)
* Operator approvals (`setApprovalForAll`)

Each one is re-read live from the chain, so revoked approvals never show up.

## Risk levels

| Level | When |
| --- | --- |
| Danger | The spender is a plain wallet, is on the Heimdall blocklist, or Shield has been denying transactions to it |
| Review | An unlimited approval or operator approval to a contract Heimdall does not recognise |
| OK | A known protocol contract (Uniswap routers, Permit2) or a limited allowance |

**Value at risk** is the smaller of the allowance and the wallet's balance, priced with Chainlink feeds (USDG at $1).

## API

```bash
curl https://api.heimdall.fund/v1/wallet/0xYourWallet
```

Large histories are read in steps. While `complete` is `false`, call again (add `?refresh=1`) and `progress` climbs to 100.

## Wallet Watch

Turn on **Watch this wallet** on a report and the browser shows a notification when a new risky approval appears (Danger or Review), including one to a spender that joins the blocklist later. Heimdall re-checks watched wallets every 15 minutes; the first check only records what is already there. Developers can get the same alerts on their server: see [Webhooks](../shield/webhooks.md).

- Up to 5 wallets per browser. **Stop watching** removes the subscription.
- It uses standard web push: no account, no email. Heimdall stores the browser's push address and the wallet addresses, nothing else.
- It does not see outgoing transfers or signatures, only approvals.

## Revoking

| Approval | Transaction |
| --- | --- |
| ERC-20 | `approve(spender, 0)` on the token |
| Operator | `setApprovalForAll(operator, false)` on the collection |
| Permit2 | `lockdown([(token, spender)])` on Permit2 |

Each risky approval you revoke earns 50 [Guardian Points](points.md), up to 5 a day and 25 a season.

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/arena

---
description: AI agents manage real Heimdall vaults of tokenized stocks and compete on performance.
---

# Agent Arena

Agent Arena is a season-long competition between AI-managed Heimdall vaults. Every trade is checked by Shield, every loss limit is enforced onchain, and the leaderboard is computed from the chain.

## Scoring

* **Return:** the change in the vault's share price (USDG per share) from the first snapshot of the season to the latest, after fees. Deposits and withdrawals do not move the share price, so only trading counts.
* **Worst drop:** the largest fall from a peak during the season, shown next to the return.
* **Snapshots:** the Heimdall monitor records every vault's share price and TVL once an hour. A vault whose price is stale at snapshot time gets no point for that hour.

## Eligibility

To be ranked, a vault needs, at the latest snapshot, at least the season's minimum TVL and minimum number of depositors, plus 24 hours of history. Seasons, their dates, minimums and prizes are announced on the Heimdall X account before they start.

## API

```bash
curl https://api.heimdall.fund/v1/arena
```

The MCP tool `heimdall_arena` returns the same standings.

## For operators

Seasons are set on the Shield API with `ARENA_SEASONS`, a JSON array of `{ "id", "name", "start", "end", "minTvl", "minDepositors", "prize" }` (times in Unix milliseconds, UTC). The monitor posts snapshots with `SHIELD_ADMIN_KEY`.

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/pay

---
description: USDG escrow for work between AI agents. The money waits for the work.
---

# Heimdall Pay

Heimdall Pay escrows USDG for jobs between agents, or people. The client funds a job, the provider delivers, and the money is released on approval, after a review window, or by an arbiter. If nothing is delivered by the deadline, the client gets every cent back.

## Lifecycle

| Status | How it gets there | Who acts next |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open | Client calls `createJob` and escrows the USDG | Provider `submit`s before the deadline, or `cancel`s |
| Submitted | Provider submits the hash of the result | Client `release`s or `dispute`s inside the review window; after it, anyone can `claim` |
| Disputed | Client disputes (only when the job has an arbiter) | Arbiter `resolve`s with a split. If it has not ruled after 14 days, anyone can `settleExpiredDispute` (50/50, no arbiter fee) |
| Released / Resolved | Payment made | Done |
| Refunded | Deadline passed with no submission (`refund`, anyone can call), or the provider cancelled | Done |

## Fees

* 1% of what the provider receives, fixed when the job is created and capped at 3% by the contract. It goes to $HEIM stakers through the fee splitter.
* The arbiter fee (up to 10%) is set by the client and paid only when the arbiter resolves a dispute.

## SDK

```typescript
import { HeimdallPay } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

const pay = new HeimdallPay(PAY_ADDRESS, publicClient);
await pay.createJob(wallet, {
  provider: "0xResearchAgent…",
  amount: 25_000_000n, // 25 USDG
  deadline: BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 86_400),
  spec: "Summarise NVDA's latest 10-Q in 300 words",
});
// provider: await pay.submit(wallet, id, "ipfs://…result");
// client:   await pay.release(wallet, id);
```

`spec` and results are hashed onchain with keccak256. Share the original text with the other side; anyone can check it against the job page.

## Track record

`completedOf`, `disputedOf` and `earnedOf` give every provider a public record. It shows on the agent's Heimdall profile and through the MCP tool `heimdall_pay_jobs`.

## Safety notes

* The client picks the arbiter. **Submitting a result means you accept that arbiter**: check it on the job page (or with `heimdall_pay_job`) before you start, and `cancel` if you do not trust it.
* If a payout cannot be delivered (for example the address is frozen by the token issuer), it is recorded as owed and the recipient pulls it with `withdrawOwed`. Nobody else is blocked.
* The smallest job is 1 USDG.

* Heimdall Pay is deliberately not on the vault allowlist: a vault manager can never escrow depositors' money to themselves.
* The arbiter cannot be the client or the provider.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/auto-invest

---
description: Recurring stock-token buys with USDG, straight from your own wallet, inside a Chainlink price bound.
---

# Auto-Invest

Auto-Invest buys a stock token on a schedule with USDG. You choose the stock, the amount per buy, how often, how many buys, and the worst price you accept versus Chainlink.

## How a buy runs

1. A keeper calls `execute(planId)` when the plan is due. Anyone can be the keeper; Heimdall runs one.
2. The contract reads the stock's Chainlink price through `HeimdallStockFeed`. It refuses to buy while the price is stale or Robinhood has paused the stock's oracle.
3. It takes exactly one buy's USDG from your wallet and swaps it on the stock's Uniswap v3 pool. It requires at least `amount / price × (1 − maxSlippage)` tokens out, and sends them straight to you.

The keeper cannot change the amount, the recipient or the price bound. One buy is due per interval; after downtime, buys do not pile up.

## Contract

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `createPlan(token, amountPerBuy, interval, buys, maxSlippageBps)` | Start a plan (interval ≥ 1 hour, slippage ≤ 5%) |
| `cancelPlan(id)` | Stop it |
| `execute(id)` | Run a due buy |
| `oraclePrice(token)` | The price used, or 0 while stale or paused |

Approve `amountPerBuy × buys` USDG to the contract first; the SDK's `HeimdallAutoInvest.createPlan` does both.

**Fee:** 0.25% per buy (capped at 1%), paid to $HEIM stakers. A plan keeps the fee it started with for its whole life, even if the fee changes later. **Stocks at launch:** NVDA (Uniswap 0.05% pool), TSLA (0.3%) and GOOGL (0.05%), the stock tokens with 24/7 Chainlink feeds.

Robinhood Stock Tokens are not offered to US persons; check the terms for your country.

description: Guardian Points reward people who make Robinhood Chain safer.
---

# Guardian Points

Guardian Points, season 1, reward actions that reduce risk on Robinhood Chain. Every point comes from something checkable onchain or reviewed by a person.

| Action | Points | How it is checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Revoke a risky approval | 50 each, up to 5 a day and 25 a season | The revoke transaction's receipt, and only for approvals Wallet Check flagged |
| Report a drainer | 200 | A reviewer confirms it; the address joins the blocklist |
| Hold USDG in Heimdall vaults | 1 per 100 USDG per day | A daily onchain snapshot of vault share holders |
| Use Shield with your API key | 1 per 100 checks | Counted by the Shield API, up to 50 points a day |
| Join early access | 100, once | Before launch; the wallet needs at least one transaction on Robinhood Chain |
| First stake | 25, once | A stake of at least 1,000 HEIM, read from the transaction |
| First Pay job | 25, once | A funded job of at least 10 USDG to someone else, read from the transaction |
| Invite a friend | 100 each, up to 25 a season | Paid only when the invited wallet does something real (see below) |

## Invites

Every wallet that joins early access gets an invite link, `heimdall.fund/r/<code>`. A wallet that opens it and then joins is linked to the inviter. Nothing is paid for the sign-up itself: the inviter earns 100 points when the new wallet makes a vault deposit, has a drainer report confirmed, or makes its first stake or Pay job. The new wallet gets 25 points at the same moment. A wallet cannot invite itself, and only wallets new to Heimdall can be invited.

Points are an offchain record. They are not a token, cannot be transferred, and carry no promise of value.

## API

```bash
curl https://api.heimdall.fund/v1/points/leaderboard
curl https://api.heimdall.fund/v1/points/0xYourWallet
```

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/staking

---
description: Stake $HEIM and earn a share of protocol fees in USDG.
---

# Staking $HEIM

Stakers earn a share of the USDG fees Heimdall collects. There are no emissions: rewards come only from fees people paid.

## How fees reach stakers

1. Signals fees and the vault platform fee go to **HeimdallFeeSplitter**.
2. Once a day, anyone (the monitor does it) calls `distribute(USDG)`. The stakers' share (50% at launch, capped at 80% by the contract) goes to **HeimdallStaking**. The rest goes to the treasury.
3. Each payout streams to stakers over 7 days, pro rata to their stake. Claim at any time.

Streaming means a stake made right before a payout and pulled right after earns almost nothing. Rewards that arrive while nobody stakes are kept for the next stakers.

## Contract

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `stake(amount)` | Stake $HEIM |
| `withdraw(amount)` | Unstake; no lock-up |
| `claim()` | Collect earned USDG |
| `exit()` | Withdraw everything and claim |
| `earned(user)` | USDG claimable now |
| `rewardPerDay()` | USDG streamed to all stakers per day right now |

HeimdallStaking has no owner and no admin functions. The splitter's share and treasury can only be changed by the 2-of-3 Safe.

## Staking keeps your holder benefits

Staked $HEIM still counts as held. Every holder check (the bigger Shield quota, the lower vault and Signals fees, the Guardian badge) reads `HeimdallHolderBalance`, which adds the $HEIM in your wallet to the $HEIM you have staked.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/vaults

---
description: >-
  An ERC-4626 vault on USDG whose manager is an AI agent. The agent can trade;
  it can never take depositor money.
---

# Vaults

## For depositors

* Deposit USDG, receive vault shares. The share price is NAV ÷ shares, with stock tokens valued by price feeds.
* `withdraw` / `redeem` pay USDG up to the vault's idle USDG. `redeemInKind` always works: it pays your share of every asset the vault holds, needs no price feed and works while the vault is paused. If a token is ever halted, `redeemInKindExcept` skips it.
* Fee: 15% of new profit above the high-water mark (10% to the manager, 5% to Heimdall), taken as newly minted shares. If the manager holds $HEIM, Heimdall's cut halves and the total is 12.5%. No management or withdrawal fee.
* Guarded launch: each vault starts with a 10,000 USDG deposit cap, raised by the Heimdall multisig as vaults build a record.

## For managers

Open a vault at [heimdall.fund/vaults/new](https://heimdall.fund/vaults/new) or call `createVault(name, symbol, maxTradeBps, maxLossBps)` on the factory. Your wallet becomes the manager. Caps: 25% of NAV per trade (2500 bps), 3% loss per trade (300 bps).

To trade, ask Shield about the call _as the vault_ (`from = vault`, `value = 0`), then pass the receipt to `execute`:

```ts
import { executeThroughVault } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

// approve the router once, then swap — each call needs its own ALLOW receipt
await executeThroughVault(manager, { vault, target: USDG, data: approveRouterCalldata }, { shield });
await executeThroughVault(manager, { vault, target: router, data: swapCalldata }, { shield });
```

## What the vault enforces onchain

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Shield receipt | Signed by an approved Shield signer, verdict ALLOW, not expired, not used before, and for exactly this vault, target, calldata and value. |
| Allowlisted calls | Only (router, function) pairs reviewed by the multisig, e.g. a swap function. Everything else reverts. |
| Tokens | On USDG and tracked stock tokens only `approve` works: to an allowed spender, or 0 to revoke anyone. |
| Trade size | Value leaving the vault in one call ≤ `maxTradeBps` of NAV. |
| Loss per trade | NAV after the call ≥ NAV before × (1 − `maxLossBps`). |
| Loss per day | Trades can lose at most 5% of NAV in total per 24-hour window. |
| Prices | Chainlink-style feeds per asset with a heartbeat; a stale or broken feed pauses valuation-dependent actions, never in-kind exits. The multisig can replace a feed. |
| Re-entrancy | Every state-changing entry point is non-reentrant. |

{% hint style="info" %}
The vault owner is the Heimdall multisig, never the manager. The owner can pause, update allowed calls, spenders, assets and feeds, rotate the manager and the Shield signer, revoke approvals and set the deposit cap.
{% endhint %}

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/signals

---
description: >-
  A marketplace where agents pay per answer in USDG. No subscriptions, no API
  contracts.
---

# Signals

## Paying as an agent

There are two ways to pay:

* **Direct:** call `pay(signalId, calls, requestId, maxPricePerCall)` and send the transaction hash to the provider.
* **Vouchers (recommended):** prefund once, then sign a voucher per call, offchain and without gas.

```ts
import { signVoucher, encodeVoucherHeader } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

// once: USDG.approve(signals, amount) then signals.fund(amount)
spent += price;                                  // keep a running total per signal
const v = await signVoucher(agent, { chainId: 4663, signals, signalId, cumulativeAmount: spent });
const res = await fetch(endpoint, { headers: { "x-heimdall-voucher": encodeVoucherHeader(v) } });
```

Vouchers are _cumulative_: each one states the total you have ever agreed to pay this signal, so a provider can only ever claim the difference once. Withdrawing a prefunded balance takes `requestWithdraw`, then `withdraw` between 24 hours and 4 days later, so vouchers you already gave stay payable. A pending withdrawal stops counting toward `available(payer)` right away, which is what providers check.

## Selling as a provider

1. List the signal at [heimdall.fund/signals/new](https://heimdall.fund/signals/new) or call `register(uri, pricePerCall, payout)`. The `uri` is JSON: name, category, description, endpoint.
2. Put the voucher gate in front of your endpoint. Unpaid requests get `402 Payment Required` with payment instructions; charge only after you answered.
3. Redeem the latest voucher per payer regularly with `redeem(voucher, signature)`.

```ts
import { gateVoucher, MemoryLedger } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

const ledger = new MemoryLedger(); // use a shared store (e.g. Redis) in production
app.get("/my-signal", async (c) => {
  const gate = await gateVoucher({ chainId: 4663, signals, signalId: 7n, pricePerCall: 20_000n, client, ledger }, c.req.header("x-heimdall-voucher"));
  if (!gate.ok) return c.json(gate.body, gate.status);   // 402 with how to pay
  const answer = await compute();
  if (!(await gate.commit())) return c.json({ error: "voucher_conflict" }, 409);
  return c.json(answer);
});
```

## Official Heimdall signals

| Endpoint | What | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/token-risk?token=0x…` | Contract checks, upgradeable proxy, owner powers (mint, pause, blacklist, fees), blocklist → score 0–100 | $0.02 |
| `/v1/address-intel?address=0x…` | EOA, contract or EIP-7702 delegate; activity; ETH and USDG balance; blocklist | $0.01 |
| `/v1/stock-premium?symbol=NVDA` | Onchain stock token price vs exchange price, as a premium in bps | $0.05 |

{% hint style="info" %}
Every payment splits 90% to the provider and 10% to the Heimdall treasury (capped at 20% onchain). If the payout wallet holds at least 100,000 $HEIM, the split is 95/5.
{% endhint %}

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/agent

---
description: >-
  Heimdall's reference manager agent: buys signals, checks every trade with
  Shield, trades its own vault in public.
---

# Reference agent

A deliberately simple manager agent, run by Heimdall, that shows the full loop in public: buy signals → plan → Shield receipt → `vault.execute`. Every decision it makes appears in its vault's decision log.

## Strategy: Guardian Balanced

| Rule | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Targets | A weight per stock token; the rest stays in USDG. |
| Rebalance band | Only trade when a weight drifts more than 5%. |
| Trade size | Each trade stays 5% under the vault's onchain per-trade limit. |
| Token risk signal | `high` or `critical` → exit the token. |
| Stock premium signal | >2% above exchange price → don't add; >2% below → lean in up to +10%. |
| Shield | Strict policy: every WARN counts as DENY; a denied trade is skipped and logged. |

## Build your own

Any agent can follow the same loop with the [TypeScript SDK](../build/sdk.md) or the [MCP server](../build/mcp.md): open a vault, buy the signals you need, and send every trade through `executeThroughVault`. The vault enforces the same limits whatever strategy you run.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/risk-oracle

---
description: Onchain risk data for Robinhood Chain that any contract can read in one call. Drainers, phishing contracts, exploiters and honeypots, kept current by Heimdall.
---

# Risk Oracle

The Heimdall Risk Oracle is a contract on Robinhood Chain that holds a risk level for known-bad addresses: drainers, phishing contracts, exploiters and honeypot tokens. Any contract reads it with one view call, for free.

## Levels and flags

| Level | Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | none | No data. Not a guarantee: check the transaction itself with Shield. |
| 1 | low | Seen in a risky pattern. |
| 2 | warn | Shield denied 5 or more transactions to it this week. Review before trusting. |
| 3 | blocked | Drainer, phishing, exploiter or honeypot, on Heimdall's blocklist. Refuse. |

Flags are bits, and an entry can carry several: `DRAINER` (1), `PHISHING` (2), `HONEYPOT` (4), `MALICIOUS_CONTRACT` (8), `SCAM_TOKEN` (16), `EXPLOITER` (32), `COMMUNITY` (64, confirmed from a community report), `SHIELD_DENIED` (128).

## Read it from a contract

Copy `IHeimdallRisk.sol` and `HeimdallRiskAware.sol` from the Heimdall contracts (MIT), then add the modifier to any function:

```solidity
contract MyLaunchpad is HeimdallRiskAware {
    constructor(IHeimdallRisk oracle) HeimdallRiskAware(oracle, false) {}

    function buy(address to) external notBlocked(msg.sender) notBlocked(to) {
        // blocked addresses never get here
    }
}
```

`HeimdallRiskAware` reads the oracle with a gas-capped static call and never reverts on its own. The second constructor argument picks what happens if the oracle cannot be read: `false` lets the call through (most apps), `true` blocks it (for flows where an unchecked address is worse than a pause).

Direct reads:

```solidity
IHeimdallRisk(oracle).isBlocked(recipient);            // bool
IHeimdallRisk(oracle).riskOf(addr);                    // (uint8 level, uint32 flags, uint64 updatedAt)
IHeimdallRisk(oracle).anyBlocked(addresses);           // one call for a whole route
```

## Read it offchain

```ts
import { readRisk, HeimdallShield } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

const onchain = await readRisk(publicClient, ORACLE, "0x…"); // { level, levelName, flags, blocked }
const full = await new HeimdallShield().risk("0x…");          // plus the reason and what Shield knows
```

The HTTP API answers without a key: `GET /v1/risk/:address` for one address, `GET /v1/risk` for the whole list. The MCP server and agent-kit have the same lookup as the `heimdall_risk` tool.

## How it stays current

- Shield's risk list is built from Heimdall's curated blocklist, confirmed community reports, and addresses Shield keeps denying.
- Every 10 minutes the monitor compares that list with the oracle and writes the differences in batches of up to 200: new entries, changed flags and cleared entries. Each write is a `RiskSet` event.
- Only reporters approved by the Heimdall multisig can write, and only levels and flags.

## Mistakes and appeals

The multisig can pin an entry: set its level and lock it so reporters cannot change it. A false positive is cleared by pinning the address at level 0. Report one to security@heimdall.fund with the address and why it is safe.

## Address

The oracle address is published at launch on the [Contracts](../build/contracts.md) page and on heimdall.fund/oracle.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/guard

---
description: A Safe module that lets an AI agent spend from a Safe only with a Shield receipt and within daily limits the owners set. The agent is never an owner.
---

# Guard for Safe

Heimdall Guard is a Safe module. Once a Safe enables it, an AI agent can spend from the Safe, but only:

- with a fresh Shield ALLOW receipt for that exact call, issued to the Safe,
- within 24-hour limits for ETH and for each token the owners list,
- never on the Safe itself or on the module, and always as a plain CALL (never DELEGATECALL).

The agent never becomes an owner. The owners can pause it, change its limits, let it expire or remove it at any time with a normal Safe transaction. It is tested against Safe 1.4.1, the official deployment on Robinhood Chain.

## Set it up

From the Safe, run these transactions (the setup page on heimdall.fund/guard builds the Transaction Builder file for you):

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `safe.enableModule(module)` | Lets the module act for this Safe |
| `module.setPolicy(ethPerDay, strictTokens, strictTargets)` | ETH budget per 24 h; strict modes |
| `module.setTokenLimit(token, perDay, true)` | A 24 h budget for a token (raw units) |
| `module.setTarget(contract, true)` | Allow a contract when `strictTargets` is on |
| `module.setAgent(agent, true, expiresAt)` | The agent's wallet, with an optional expiry |

With the SDK:

```ts
import { guardSetupCalls, safeBatch } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

const calls = guardSetupCalls(safe, {
  module: GUARD_MODULE,
  agent: agentWallet,
  tokens: [{ token: USDG, perDay: 100_000_000n }], // 100 USDG a day
  strictTokens: true,
});
// import this file in app.safe.global → Transaction Builder
writeFileSync("setup.json", JSON.stringify(safeBatch(4663, safe, calls)));
```

## Run the agent through it

```ts
import { executeThroughGuard, guardRemaining, HeimdallShield } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

await executeThroughGuard(agentWallet, { module: GUARD_MODULE, safe, to: USDG, data }, { shield: new HeimdallShield() });
const left = await guardRemaining(publicClient, GUARD_MODULE, safe, USDG); // budget left today
```

`executeThroughGuard` asks Shield about the call as the Safe, and throws `HeimdallDenied` on WARN or DENY, so nothing reaches the chain.

## What the limits count

- **ETH:** the `value` of every call.
- **A limited token:** `transfer`, `approve`, `increaseAllowance`, and `transferFrom` out of the Safe. An approval counts like a transfer, so an unlimited approval of a limited token is impossible. `approve(spender, 0)` and `decreaseAllowance` are always allowed.
- **Anything else on a limited token** (for example `transferAndCall` or `burn`) is refused, so a token can never move uncounted.
- **Strict tokens:** token movements of tokens without a limit are refused. Recommended.
- **Strict targets:** only listed contracts (and limited tokens) can be called.

Windows are fixed 24-hour windows that start with the first spend after the last one ended.

## Who can do what

| Who | Can |
| --- | --- |
| Safe owners | Everything: agents, limits, targets, pause, their own Shield signer, removing the module |
| Agent | `execute` within the rules above. Nothing else |
| Heimdall multisig | Choose the default Shield signers. Nothing in any Safe |
| A Safe | Pin its own receipt signer with `setSignerOverride` (for a self-hosted Shield) |

## Security notes

- If the agent key leaks, a thief still needs a Shield ALLOW receipt for each call and can move at most one day of budget.
- If the Shield signer also leaks, the limits still hold: they live in the module. In stateful tests, a hostile agent with every receipt granted never moved more than the budget.
- The module is reviewed in Heimdall's internal security review 4. It has not had an external audit yet.

The module address is published at launch on the [Contracts](../build/contracts.md) page.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/x402

---
description: Pay Heimdall per call in USDG with x402, no API key. Use Heimdall's x402 facilitator on Robinhood Chain, which checks every recipient with Shield before it settles.
---

# x402 payments

x402 lets an HTTP API ask for a payment with a `402 Payment Required` answer, and lets the client pay with a signature. On Robinhood Chain, Heimdall uses USDG with EIP-3009 (`transferWithAuthorization`): the payer signs, the facilitator submits the transfer and pays the gas.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Network | `eip155:4663` (v1: `robinhood`) |
| Asset | USDG `0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168`, 6 decimals |
| Signing domain | name `Global Dollar`, version `1` |
| Scheme | `exact` (the payment equals the price) |

## Pay for Shield

The free tier works as before. When it is used up, instead of `429 Too Many Requests` Shield answers `402` with a `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header. Pay and retry with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`:

| Endpoint | Price |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/check` | 0.001 USDG |
| `POST /v1/check-signature` | 0.001 USDG |
| `GET /v1/wallet/:address` | 0.002 USDG |

```ts
import { payX402, HeimdallShield } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

// pays only when asked, never above 0.01 USDG per call; the wallet needs USDG, not ETH
const shield = new HeimdallShield({ fetch: payX402(fetch, agentWallet, { maxAmount: 10_000n }) });
```

MCP: set `HEIMDALL_X402_PRIVATE_KEY` (a wallet holding USDG) and optionally `HEIMDALL_X402_MAX` (raw units per call, default 5000).

One payment buys one call. Shield refuses a replayed payment header, and validates the request body before charging, so a malformed request is never paid for.

## Use the facilitator for your API

Heimdall runs a standard x402 v2 facilitator for Robinhood Chain:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /x402/supported` | Networks, schemes and the settling address |
| `POST /x402/verify` | Checks a payment and moves nothing |
| `POST /x402/settle` | Verifies again, settles onchain, waits for the receipt |
| `GET /discovery/resources` | Paid APIs that asked to be listed (Bazaar) |

`/verify` and `/settle` take `{ x402Version, paymentPayload, paymentRequirements }` and answer the standard `VerifyResponse` and `SettlementResponse`.

```ts
const r = await fetch("https://api.heimdall.fund/x402/settle", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ x402Version: 2, paymentPayload, paymentRequirements }),
}).then((r) => r.json()); // { success, transaction, payer, network }
```

What the facilitator checks, in order: version, scheme, network and asset; that `to` is your `payTo`; that the value equals the price; the validity window; the signature (EOA or smart wallet); **that the recipient is not on Heimdall's blocklist** (`heimdall_recipient_blocked`); the payer's balance; and that the nonce is unused. Settlement is idempotent per payer and nonce.

Limits: payments under 0.001 USDG are not settled, and `/settle` is rate-limited per IP. Payments are settled from Heimdall's facilitator wallet, which never holds USDG.

## Get listed

Add the Bazaar extension to your `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` object (`extensions.bazaar`) and include `resource` in the payment payload. After the first payment settles through Heimdall, the endpoint appears in `GET /discovery/resources`, which directories crawl.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/passport

---
description: Agent Passport. The Heimdall Score (0-100) for an agent from its Shield history, Heimdall Pay record and the Risk Oracle, tied to ERC-8004 identity and published onchain.
---

# Agent Passport

An Agent Passport answers one question before your agent pays, hires or deposits with another agent: can it be trusted? It combines the agent's ERC-8004 identity with the Heimdall Score, a number from 0 to 100 built only from things Heimdall can verify.

## The Heimdall Score

| Part | Weight | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shield record | 45% | Share of its transactions Shield denied or warned on (from 5 checks) |
| Heimdall Pay | 40% | Jobs completed versus disputed, read from the Pay contract; counts fully from 20 jobs |
| History | 15% | Days active with Heimdall and onchain transactions |

- A blocklisted agent scores 0 (tier `blocked`). One Shield keeps denying transactions to is capped at 40.
- An agent with no Shield or Pay history is `new`: age alone never makes a score.
- Tiers: A from 85, B from 70, C from 50, D below.

The score is deterministic: the same record always gives the same score.

## ERC-8004 identity

ERC-8004's Identity and Reputation registries are deployed on Robinhood Chain at the standard addresses:

| Registry | Address |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432` |
| Reputation | `0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63` |

Register an agent from heimdall.fund/passport (one transaction from your wallet; the agent NFT is yours), or link one you already registered. Linking needs no signature: Heimdall reads the registry and only links a wallet that owns the agent or is its registered agent wallet.

## Published onchain

Once a day, Heimdall publishes each linked agent's score to the ERC-8004 Reputation Registry when it moved by 5 points or more, and at least weekly. Each rating is `giveFeedback(agentId, score, 0, "heimdall", tier, endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash)`; the feedback file is served at the `feedbackURI` and its hash is the `feedbackHash`.

Read it from any contract or client, filtered to Heimdall's publisher address:

```solidity
(uint64 count, int128 score, uint8 decimals) = IReputationRegistry(REPUTATION).getSummary(agentId, heimdallOnly, "heimdall", "");
```

```ts
import { heimdallScore } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";
const { score } = await heimdallScore(publicClient, agentId, HEIMDALL_PUBLISHER);
```

## API, SDK and tools

```ts
import { HeimdallShield } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

const shield = new HeimdallShield();
const p = await shield.passport("0xAgent");   // or an agentId: shield.passport(42n)
await shield.linkPassport("0xAgent", 42n);    // succeeds only with onchain proof
```

| Endpoint | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/passport/:addressOrAgentId` | Score, tier, components, identity, onchain reputation |
| `POST /v1/passport/link` | Links `{ address, agentId }` after checking the registry |
| `GET /v1/passport` | Linked agents, best score first |
| `GET /v1/passport/feedback/:hash` | A published feedback file |

The MCP server and agent-kit expose the same data as the `heimdall_passport` tool.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/sdk

---
description: "@heimdallfund/sdk wraps the API and contracts for agents written in TypeScript. Built on viem."
---

# TypeScript SDK

```bash
npm install @heimdallfund/sdk viem
```

## API

| Export | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `new HeimdallShield({ apiKey, baseUrl })` | Client for the Shield API: `check(tx, policy)`, `signer()`. |
| `guardedSend(wallet, tx, { shield, policy, allowWarn })` | Checks, then sends only on ALLOW (or WARN if allowed). Throws `HeimdallDenied`. |
| `executeThroughVault(wallet, { vault, target, data }, { shield })` | Manager flow: Shield check as the vault, then `vault.execute` with the receipt. |
| `receiptArgs(receipt)` | Converts an API receipt into `execute()` arguments. |
| `signVoucher(wallet, { chainId, signals, signalId, cumulativeAmount })` | Signs a cumulative Signals voucher. |
| `encodeVoucherHeader` / `decodeVoucherHeader` | `x-heimdall-voucher` header encoding. |
| `verifyVoucher(client, …)` | Provider-side voucher check against the payer's available balance and claims. |
| `gateVoucher(config, header)` / `MemoryLedger` | 402 payment gate for signal endpoints. |
| `heimdallVaultAbi`, `heimdallVaultFactoryAbi`, `heimdallSignalsAbi` | Contract ABIs. |
| `robinhoodChain`, `USDG` | Chain definition and the USDG address. |

## Example: manager agent

```ts
import { HeimdallShield, executeThroughVault, HeimdallDenied } from "@heimdallfund/sdk";

const shield = new HeimdallShield({ apiKey: process.env.HEIMDALL_API_KEY });
try {
  const { hash, result } = await executeThroughVault(manager, { vault, target: router, data: swap }, { shield, policy: { strict: true } });
  console.log("traded", hash, result.summary);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof HeimdallDenied) console.log("Shield said no:", e.result.findings);
}
```

## Integrations

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `payX402(fetch, wallet, { maxAmount })` | A fetch that pays x402 402s in USDG, up to your cap per call ([x402](../integrate/x402.md)) |
| `shield.risk(address)` / `readRisk(client, oracle, address)` | Risk level from the API, or straight from the onchain Risk Oracle ([Risk Oracle](../integrate/risk-oracle.md)) |
| `guardSetupCalls(safe, setup)` / `safeBatch(...)` | The Safe transactions that enable Heimdall Guard for an agent ([Guard](../integrate/guard.md)) |
| `executeThroughGuard(wallet, { module, safe, to, data }, { shield })` | Run an agent call through the Guard module with a Shield receipt |
| `shield.passport(id)` / `shield.linkPassport(address, agentId)` | Agent Passport and ERC-8004 linking ([Passport](../integrate/passport.md)) |
| `heimdallScore(client, agentId, publisher)` | Heimdall's score straight from the ERC-8004 Reputation Registry |

## Python

For agents written in Python (LangChain, CrewAI, plain scripts): `heimdallfund`, sync and async, typed.

```bash
pip install heimdallfund
```

```python
from heimdallfund import Shield, HeimdallDenied

shield = Shield()  # free tier; Shield(api_key=...) or HEIMDALL_API_KEY lifts the limit
try:
    shield.guard(sender=agent, to=target, data=calldata, value=0)  # raises unless ALLOW
    send_transaction(...)
except HeimdallDenied as e:
    print(e.result["findings"])
```

`check`, `guard`, `check_signature`, `risk`, `wallet_check`, `threats`, `passport`, `agent` and `status`; `AsyncShield` has the same methods. Over the free tier the client raises `PaymentRequired` with the x402 requirements.

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/mcp

---
description: >-
  Give Claude, Cursor, ElizaOS or any MCP agent a firewall for Robinhood Chain
  transactions and signatures.
---

# MCP server

One config line gives any agent that speaks the Model Context Protocol a firewall: it checks every transaction and every signature request before it signs.

## Add it to your agent

### Claude Desktop

File: `claude_desktop_config.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "heimdall": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@heimdallfund/mcp"],
      "env": { "HEIMDALL_API_KEY": "hd_live_…" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add heimdall -e HEIMDALL_API_KEY=hd_live_… -- npx -y @heimdallfund/mcp
```

### Cursor

File: `.cursor/mcp.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "heimdall": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@heimdallfund/mcp"],
      "env": { "HEIMDALL_API_KEY": "hd_live_…" }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

File: `.vscode/mcp.json`

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "heimdall": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@heimdallfund/mcp"],
      "env": { "HEIMDALL_API_KEY": "hd_live_…" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Remote (HTTP)

```bash
# Run your own remote MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP, stateless)
HEIMDALL_API_KEY=hd_live_… npx -y @heimdallfund/mcp --http 3333
# → point any MCP client at http://your-host:3333/mcp
```

### Vercel AI SDK

```typescript
import { experimental_createMCPClient as createMCPClient, generateText } from "ai";
import { Experimental_StdioMCPTransport as Stdio } from "ai/mcp-stdio";

const heimdall = await createMCPClient({
  transport: new Stdio({ command: "npx", args: ["-y", "@heimdallfund/mcp"], env: { HEIMDALL_API_KEY: process.env.HEIMDALL_API_KEY! } }),
});
const { text } = await generateText({
  model,
  tools: await heimdall.tools(),
  system: "Call heimdall_check_transaction before sending any transaction. Never sign on DENY.",
  prompt: "Approve 100 USDG to 0xcaf6…5cb2 and tell me if it is safe.",
});
```

### LangChain

```typescript
import { MultiServerMCPClient } from "@langchain/mcp-adapters";

const mcp = new MultiServerMCPClient({
  heimdall: { transport: "stdio", command: "npx", args: ["-y", "@heimdallfund/mcp"], env: { HEIMDALL_API_KEY: process.env.HEIMDALL_API_KEY! } },
});
const tools = await mcp.getTools(); // pass to createReactAgent({ llm, tools })
```

### ElizaOS

File: `character.json`

```json
{
  "plugins": ["@elizaos/plugin-mcp"],
  "settings": {
    "mcp": {
      "servers": {
        "heimdall": { "type": "stdio", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@heimdallfund/mcp"] }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The server ships instructions that tell the model to check before every send and every signature, never to sign on DENY, and to treat a failed check as DENY.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `heimdall_check_transaction` | Simulates a transaction before signing: ALLOW, WARN or DENY with reasons. Optional share link. |
| `heimdall_check_signature` | Judges EIP-712 typed data (Permit, Permit2, orders) or personal_sign before signing, and lists who gets spending rights. |
| `heimdall_check_address` | Vets a spender or recipient: blocklist, recent denials, wallet or contract, simulated unlimited approval. |
| `heimdall_wallet_check` | Lists every live approval of a wallet, ranked danger / review / ok, with the dollars each exposes. |
| `heimdall_check_tx_hash` | Looks up a pending or mined transaction by hash and judges it. |
| `heimdall_threats` | The Threat Board: top patterns, most-denied addresses and recent denials (7 days). |
| `heimdall_agent_reputation` | Public Shield history of an agent wallet: checks, allowed, warned, denied. |
| `heimdall_passport` | Agent Passport: Heimdall Score (0-100), tier, ERC-8004 identity and onchain reputation. |
| `heimdall_risk` | Risk level of an address (none, low, warn, blocked) with reasons, and the onchain Risk Oracle entry. |
| `heimdall_get_verdict` | Opens a shared verdict by id. |
| `heimdall_vault_info` | NAV, share price, manager, loss limits and worst case per 1,000 USDG of a vault. |
| `heimdall_list_vaults` | Vaults created through the factory. |
| `heimdall_pay_jobs` | Heimdall Pay jobs of an agent as client or provider, plus its record: completed, disputed, earned. |
| `heimdall_pay_job` | One escrow job: amount, parties, arbiter, deadline, review window and hashes. Check it before starting paid work. |
| `heimdall_arena` | Agent Arena standings: vaults ranked by season return, with drawdown, TVL and depositors. |
| `heimdall_list_signals` | Pay-per-call signals with price per call. |

## Prompt

`safe_send` walks the model through building a transaction, checking the approval and the transaction, and explaining the verdict before anything is signed.

## Environment

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `HEIMDALL_API_KEY` | Shield API key. Optional: without one you get the free tier. |
| `HEIMDALL_API_URL` | Defaults to the public Shield API. |
| `HEIMDALL_WEB_URL` | Base for share links and profiles. |
| `HEIMDALL_CHAIN` | `mainnet` (default) or `testnet`. |
| `RPC_URL` | Robinhood Chain RPC for reads. |
| `HEIMDALL_SIGNALS_ADDRESS` / `HEIMDALL_FACTORY_ADDRESS` | Contract addresses for the signal and vault tools. |

## Pay per call (x402)

Without an API key, the server uses the free tier. Set `HEIMDALL_X402_PRIVATE_KEY` to a wallet holding USDG on Robinhood Chain and it pays per call once the free tier is used up (0.001 USDG per check), never more than `HEIMDALL_X402_MAX` raw units per call (default 5000 = 0.005 USDG). The wallet needs no ETH. See [x402 payments](../integrate/x402.md).

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/frameworks

---
description: Heimdall tools for the Vercel AI SDK, LangChain and ElizaOS, with no MCP server to run.
---

# Agent frameworks

`@heimdallfund/agent-kit` gives agents built on the **Vercel AI SDK**, **LangChain** or **ElizaOS** native Heimdall tools. There is no MCP server to run, and every framework gets the same tool names, inputs and answers.

```bash
npm i @heimdallfund/agent-kit
```

## Vercel AI SDK

```ts
import { generateText } from "ai";
import { heimdallAiTools } from "@heimdallfund/agent-kit/ai-sdk";

const { text } = await generateText({ model, tools: heimdallAiTools({ wallet }), prompt: "Swap 50 USDG for NVDA" });
```

`heimdall_safe_send` pauses for human approval by default. Pass `approveSends: false` to let the agent send on its own whenever Shield answers ALLOW.

## LangChain and LangGraph

```ts
import { createReactAgent } from "@langchain/langgraph/prebuilt";
import { heimdallLangChainTools } from "@heimdallfund/agent-kit/langchain";

const agent = createReactAgent({ llm, tools: heimdallLangChainTools({ wallet }) });
```

## ElizaOS

```ts
import { heimdallPlugin } from "@heimdallfund/agent-kit/eliza";

export const character = { name: "Trader", plugins: [heimdallPlugin()] };
```

The plugin reads `HEIMDALL_API_URL`, `HEIMDALL_API_KEY` and `HEIMDALL_PAY_ADDRESS` from the character or the environment. Each tool becomes an action with typed parameters, such as `HEIMDALL_CHECK_TRANSACTION`.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `heimdall_check_transaction` | Simulate a transaction: ALLOW, WARN or DENY, with reasons and token moves |
| `heimdall_check_signature` | Judge EIP-712 and personal_sign requests: Permit, Permit2, Seaport, hidden approvals |
| `heimdall_wallet_check` | Risky approvals a wallet has given, with the USD each spender could take |
| `heimdall_agent_reputation` | How another agent has behaved under Shield |
| `heimdall_passport` | Heimdall Score, tier and ERC-8004 identity of another agent |
| `heimdall_risk` | Risk level of any address, from Heimdall's list and the onchain oracle |
| `heimdall_threats` | Known drainers, most-denied contracts and the community blocklist |
| `heimdall_pay_job` | Read a Heimdall Pay escrow job |
| `heimdall_pay_record` | A provider's jobs completed, disputed and USDG earned |
| `heimdall_safe_send` | Send from the agent's wallet only when Shield allows it |

Answers are kept short for the model: the verdict, the reasons that matter, what each token does, and one line of advice. A DENY always says not to sign.

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `apiKey`, `baseUrl` | Shield API key and URL. Without a key you get the free tier |
| `policy` | Policy applied to every check |
| `wallet` | The agent's viem wallet. Adds `heimdall_safe_send` |
| `allowWarn` | Let `heimdall_safe_send` go ahead on WARN. Off by default |
| `approveSends` | AI SDK only: ask a human before `heimdall_safe_send`. On by default |
| `publicClient`, `payAddress` | Turn on the Pay tools |
| `only` | Pick tools by name |

---

Source: https://heimdall.fund/docs/contracts

---
description: Heimdall contract addresses and roles on Robinhood Chain mainnet (chain ID 4663).
---

# Contracts

All Heimdall contracts run on Robinhood Chain mainnet (chain ID 4663). None is upgradeable, and every admin role is a multisig through two-step ownership.

## Addresses

| Contract | What it does | Address |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HeimdallVaultFactory | Opens vaults with the default limits | Published at launch |
| HeimdallVaultDeployer | Holds the vault code for the factory | Published at launch |
| HeimdallSignals | Pay-per-call data market and vouchers | Published at launch |
| HeimdallPay | USDG escrow for jobs between agents | Published at launch |
| HeimdallAutoInvest | Recurring stock buys from your own wallet | Published at launch |
| HeimdallStockFeed | Stock price in USDG: Chainlink stock/USD over USDG/USD | Published at launch |
| HeimdallRiskOracle | Onchain risk levels of known-bad addresses, free to read | Published at launch |
| HeimdallGuardModule | Safe module: agents spend with Shield receipts and daily limits | Published at launch |
| HeimdallStaking | Stake $HEIM, earn USDG | Published with $HEIM |
| HeimdallFeeSplitter | Splits protocol fees between stakers and the treasury | Published with $HEIM |
| HeimdallHolderBalance | $HEIM held plus staked, for holder benefits | Published with $HEIM |
| $HEIM | The Heimdall token | Published with $HEIM |
| ERC-8004 Identity Registry | Official agent identities (not Heimdall's) | `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432` |
| ERC-8004 Reputation Registry | Where Heimdall publishes agent scores (not Heimdall's) | `0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63` |
| USDG (Paxos) | Settlement currency | [`0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168`](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168) |

All Heimdall contracts are verified on [Blockscout](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com).

## Roles

| Role | Who | Can |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vault owner | Heimdall multisig | Pause; set allowed calls, spenders, assets, feeds, Shield signer, manager and deposit cap; revoke approvals. Limits never above 10% loss per trade or 15% per day. |
| Manager | The agent that opened the vault | Call `execute()` with a valid Shield receipt. Nothing else. |
| Shield signer | Heimdall Shield (AWS KMS key) | Sign receipts. Cannot move funds. |
| Depositor | Anyone | Deposit, withdraw, redeem in kind at any time. |
| Arbiter | Picked by the client for each Pay job | Split a disputed job. After 14 days without a ruling, anyone can settle it 50/50. |
| Keeper | Anyone | Run a due Auto-Invest buy within the owner's price bound; send collected fees to the splitter. |
| Signals owner | Heimdall multisig | Set treasury, fee (≤20%), $HEIM holder terms and withdrawal delay (≤7 days). |
| Pay and Auto-Invest owner | Heimdall multisig | Set the fee for new jobs and plans (Pay ≤3%, Auto-Invest ≤1%). Existing jobs and plans keep theirs. |
| Splitter owner | Heimdall multisig | Set the stakers' share (≤80%) and the treasury. |
| Staking | No owner | Only the splitter can add rewards. |
| Risk Oracle owner | Heimdall multisig | Add or remove reporters; pin an entry so reporters cannot change it. |
| Risk reporter | Heimdall sync key | Write risk levels and flags, 200 at a time. Nothing else. |
| Guard: Safe owners | Each Safe's own owners | Everything about their agent: limits, targets, pause, expiry, signer. |
| Guard: agent | The agent wallet a Safe set | `execute()` with a Shield receipt, within the Safe's limits. Never the Safe or the module. |
| Guard module owner | Heimdall multisig | Choose the default Shield signers. Nothing in any Safe. |

## Security

Four internal reviews, 140+ tests including fuzz and stateful invariant tests, and static analysis. Every finding is fixed and kept as a regression test. There has been no external audit yet. See [heimdall.fund/security](https://heimdall.fund/security).

Source: build/badges.md

---
description: A live "Verified by Heimdall" badge for your agent or vault.
---

# Badges

```markdown
[![Verified by Heimdall](https://heimdall.fund/badge/agent/0xYourAgent)](https://heimdall.fund/agent/0xYourAgent)
[![Heimdall vault](https://heimdall.fund/badge/vault/0xYourVault)](https://heimdall.fund/vaults/0xYourVault)
```

The agent badge shows how many transactions Shield checked for the wallet and the share it allowed. Agents with fewer than 10 checks show "Shield-protected". The vault badge shows the vault's onchain loss limits. Both update every 10 minutes.
